title: The Secret Locker
premise: Tamsin Sandoval, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, keeps to herself until an anonymous group chat begins posting predictions of school events before they happen — and one of them names her. Tracing the messages, she discovers the chat is run by a student who found a hidden locker containing records of the school's buried wrongs, including the expulsion of a girl who died by suicide years ago. As the chat's predictions escalate from pranks to dangerous sabotage, Tamsin must decide whether to protect the school's fragile order or expose the truth, all while competing for the rowing championship that determines her scholarship. In the end, she wins the race, loses the scholarship anyway for speaking out, and finds that justice — and a new identity built on honesty — was the real prize.
about_author: P. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former boarding-school teacher who spent a decade watching students keep secrets in plain sight. They write young adult fiction about ordinary kids forced to make extraordinary choices.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Establishes her careful invisibility at Ashgrove: scholarship pressure, rowing, and the unspoken rules of the wealthy students she serves lunch to. Emotional beat: quiet pride in her control, undercut by loneliness she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Prediction
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. An anonymous group chat called ORACLE posts that the fountain will run red at Friday's assembly — and it does, dyed crimson. A second message names Tamsin as the next 'chapter.' Emotional beat: the chill of being seen when she's built her life on not being.

chapters.title: Rules of the Game
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The administration interrogates rowing teammates; Tamsin lies smoothly to protect herself and notices Dev, the quiet equipment manager, lying just as smoothly. Emotional beat: the intoxicating and frightening discovery that she's good at deception.

chapters.title: ORACLE Speaks
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Revealed as a chat member, Dev recruits Tamsin with a demonstration: a prediction of the headmaster's resignation letter, dated next month. Emotional beat: temptation — someone is finally offering Tamsin a seat at the table instead of the margins.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Dev shows her the hidden locker behind the old gym wall, stuffed with decades of records: bribes, hushed scandals, and the file of Mariela Cruz, expelled in 2009, dead within a year. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Erased
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin researches Mariela and finds her mother living two towns over, still asking questions no one answered. Emotional beat: Tamsin recognizes herself in Mariela — another scholarship girl who didn't know the rules until they destroyed her.

chapters.title: Stroke Rate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Rowing intensifies as the coach, complicit in old cover-ups, pushes her toward the championship that secures her scholarship. Emotional beat: the boat as sanctuary — the one place where effort honestly equals outcome.

chapters.title: Split the Chat
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The ORACLE group fractures: some want viral spectacle, others want quiet justice for Mariela. Dev and Tamsin are outvoted by Priya, who plans to target the headmaster's family. Emotional beat: dread as a righteous cause tips toward cruelty.

chapters.title: The Wrong Target
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Priya's prank on the headmaster's daughter goes wrong; the girl is hospitalized after a panic-induced fall. Tamsin realizes ORACLE has become the thing it hated. Emotional beat: guilt — she was in the chat, she said nothing.

chapters.title: What the Scholarship Buys
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The headmaster offers Tamsin a deal: identify ORACLE's members and her tuition is guaranteed through graduation. Emotional beat: the seduction of safety, and the sick recognition that Ashgrove buys silence the same way every time.

chapters.title: Mariela's Mother
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin visits Elena Cruz, who shows her Mariela's letters — evidence that a beloved teacher falsified records to protect a donor's son. Emotional beat: Tamsin stops asking whether to act and starts asking how.

chapters.title: Double Coxswain
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev and Tamsin quietly take over ORACLE, redirecting it toward documentation instead of sabotage, while feeding Priya false targets. Emotional beat: wary partnership deepening into trust neither will admit is friendship.

chapters.title: Regatta
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The championship semifinal; Tamsin rows the race of her life while a text from ORACLE warns the coach is about to cut her. Emotional beat: fury channeled into speed — she will not be erased like Mariela.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Priya discovers the deception and leaks the locker's location to the administration, forcing Tamsin to move the evidence the night before finals. Emotional beat: terror and resolve — the archive is now the only weapon, and it's in her hands.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Cover Story
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The school throws prom to bury the scandal; Tamsin and Dev plan to project Mariela's file during the ceremony. Emotional beat: bittersweet normalcy — one slow dance that feels stolen from a life she might have had.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The headmaster catches Tamsin copying files and threatens expulsion, revealing he was a student when Mariela was expelled — and did nothing. Emotional beat: Tamsin's fear transmuting into contempt for men who protect their younger selves.

chapters.title: The Race That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Championship final. Tamsin rows knowing the result no longer determines her future — she's already decided to burn the scholarship. Emotional beat: freedom in the stroke; she wins, and it costs her nothing she values.

chapters.title: The One That Does
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. During prom, the lights die and Mariela's file fills every screen: names, dates, the falsified records. The room erupts. Emotional beat: catharsis and terror as Tamsin steps into the light and claims the act publicly.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The school suspends the headmaster; the board scrambles. Tamsin's scholarship is revoked for 'conduct violations,' exactly as she predicted. Emotional beat: the hollow cost of justice — and Dev's refusal to let her carry it alone.

chapters.title: Elena Cruz Reads the File
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin hands Elena the complete archive and a public apology drafted by the student paper. Elena finally hears her daughter's name spoken by the school. Emotional beat: grief that is, for the first time, shared instead of solitary.

chapters.title: What ORACLE Was For
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The remaining members vote to disband, leaving behind a public archive and a promise to watch. Priya, chastened, chooses restorative work over revenge. Emotional beat: the difference between justice and vengeance, finally understood.

chapters.title: Tamsin Sandoval, By Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At a new public school, Tamsin introduces herself aloud, unhidden, and joins the rowing team without a scholarship to protect. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt — she was never invisible; she was hiding, and she has stopped.
